topic: Range-based for Loop with Auto and Associative Containers
explanation: In modern C++, the range-based for loop simplifies iteration over containers, including associative containers like std::map and std::set. When combined with the auto keyword, it allows for concise, type-safe iteration without explicitly specifying iterator types. This enhances code readability and maintainability, especially when working with complex container types or custom iterators.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates a range-based for loop iterating over an std::map, an associative container. The 'auto' keyword deduces the type of each element as a const reference to a std::pair<const std::string, int>. The loop prints each key-value pair, showcasing modern C++ idioms for clean, efficient iteration over associative containers.
